text: Oriel documentation Oriel is a Shopify theme for stores that sell a focused range of carefully made products. This guide explains how to set up the theme and what each setting and section does. Before you edit code or install apps that change theme files, duplicate your theme in Online Store > Themes > … > Duplicate so you can always go back.

In Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Themes and add Oriel from the Shopify Theme Store. Click Customize to open the theme editor. Set up your menus in Content > Menus. The header uses your Main menu and the footer uses your Footer menu by default. Menus can have up to three levels: nested links open in dropdowns on desktop and in the mobile menu. Add your logo in the Header section, your favicon in Theme settings > Favicon, and links to your accounts in Theme settings > Social media. Replace the placeholder images and text in each section of the home page.

Theme settings: fonts, colors, shapes, cart and search. Header and footer: logo, menus, announcements and the footer. Sections: every section you can add to your pages. Product pages: blocks, media, variants and purchase options. Collections and search: filters, sorting and search suggestions. Quick add and cart: the cart drawer, cart page and quick add. Blog and pages: blog posts, pages, contact, 404 and password pages. Languages and markets: selling in several countries and languages. Accessibility and performance: how Oriel stays fast and accessible. FAQ and Support.
You can see your theme version in Online Store > Themes, under the theme name. Include it when you contact support.
Theme settings Theme settings apply to your whole store. Open them from the paintbrush icon in the theme editor.
Favicon image is the small icon in the browser tab. Use a square image; 32 × 32 px is recommended.

Setting What it does Headings Font for headings, the logo when you use your store name, and large wordmarks. Body Font for text, buttons and form fields. Accent Font for small labels, prices and subheadings. Heading size Scales all headings up or down. Body text size Scales body text up or down. Use uppercase accent text Shows labels and subheadings in capital letters. Fonts come from Shopify's font library, so they load quickly and don't need a license.

Page width: the maximum width of page content on large screens. Page margin: the space at the sides of the page. It scales down on smaller screens, so phones get a narrower margin. Show back to top button: a round button in the corner of long pages.

Colors are set in color schemes. Each scheme has a background, surface (cards and form fields), text, muted text, border, button and button label color. Sections and some blocks let you choose a scheme, so you can create contrast between sections without editing colors one by one. Keep enough contrast between text and background colors: 4.5:1 for text is the accessibility standard.

Setting What it does Button shape Pill, Rounded or Square. Applies to buttons, quantity selectors, option buttons and filter buttons. Color swatches stay round. Image corner radius Rounds the corners of images and cards. Input style Underline or Outline for form fields. Input corner radius Rounds the corners of outlined form fields.
Use animations turns hover and transition effects on or off. Animations are always off for visitors who ask their device to reduce motion.

Cart type chooses what happens when a customer adds a product: Drawer opens the cart in a panel at the side, and Page keeps customers where they are and shows a short message with a link to the cart. See Quick add and cart.
Show search suggestions shows products, collections, pages and articles as customers type in the search window.
Show currency codes adds the currency code to prices, for example $10.00 USD. It's recommended when you sell in more than one currency.

Add links to your Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X (Twitter), Threads, YouTube, Pinterest, Snapchat, Tumblr, Vimeo and LinkedIn accounts. Icons appear in the footer when Show social media icons is on in the footer section.
Header and footer The announcement bar, header and footer appear on every page. Edit them in the theme editor's sidebar, above and below the page sections.

Add up to eight Announcement blocks, each with text and an optional link. Use scrolling announcements: announcements scroll across the top of the page. Scrolling pauses when a customer hovers over or focuses it, and doesn't run for visitors who prefer reduced motion. Turn it off to show announcements side by side. Scroll speed: the time for one full loop. On wide screens, announcements repeat so the bar is always full.

Logo image and Logo width. Without a logo, the header shows your store name. Wide, tall and square logos all work: tall logos are limited in height so the header stays compact. Logo position: Center or Left.

Menu: the menu shown in the header. Links with nested links open a dropdown. Customer account menu: links shown in the account window, such as orders and profile. Popular searches: comma-separated search terms shown as shortcuts in the search window. Show labels next to icons: shows "Search", "Account" and "Bag" next to the icons on larger screens. Use sticky header: keeps the header at the top while customers scroll.

Mobile menu: optionally a different, shorter menu for phones. Show numbers: numbers the top-level links. Show bottom navigation on phones: a bar at the bottom of the screen with Home, Shop, Search, Account and Bag. Shop opens the mobile menu, and Bag shows the number of items in the cart. On product pages and the cart page, the add to cart and checkout bars take its place while they're shown. With the bar on, the account icon moves from the header to the bar on phones, which leaves room to center the logo.

Add Text blocks for a short brand line and Menu blocks for link columns. Show large wordmark and Wordmark text: a large line of text across the footer, your store name by default. Show country/region selector and Show language selector: appear when you sell in more than one country or language. See Languages and markets. Show social media icons, Show Follow on Shop, Show policy links and Show payment icons in the bottom bar. Note: a short line of text in the bottom bar, for example your company details. Follow on Shop only shows when Shop Pay is turned on for your store.
Sections Add sections to any page with Add section in the theme editor. Drag sections to reorder them, and use the eye icon to hide one without deleting it.

Most sections have a Section style group with Color scheme, Show divider (a line above the section), Top padding and Bottom padding. Many also have a Subheading, Heading and Text, and a Link label and Link shown beside the heading.

Section Use it for Slideshow Large images or videos, each with a subheading, heading and button. Add up to four Collection shortcut blocks to show collection thumbnails in the corner on screens 1200 px and wider. Slides change automatically every few seconds (Change slides automatically, Change slides every); a pause button is always shown, and slides don't change for visitors who prefer reduced motion. A video slide stays on screen for the length of the video. Featured collection Products from a collection as a Carousel or Grid. Show product type filter adds buttons that filter the products b

Upload images at least 2000 px wide for full-width sections. Oriel serves smaller versions to smaller screens, so large uploads don't slow your store down. Set a focal point on an image in Shopify admin to keep the important part in view when the image is cropped. Add alt text to images in Content > Files or on the product. Images without alt text are treated as decorative, so screen readers skip them.
Blog and pages

The Blog posts page lists your posts. Feature the latest post shows the newest post large at the top. Show tag filter adds buttons that filter posts by tag. Posts per page, Columns on desktop, Show date and Show excerpt set up the list. Posts use their excerpt when you've written one, or else their first paragraph.

The Blog post section can show the featured image, date, author, tags, comments and more posts from the blog (Show featured image, Show date, Show author, Show tags, Show comments, Show more posts from the blog). Comments appear when comments are turned on for the blog in Content > Blog posts > Manage blogs. When comments need approval, customers see a message saying so after they post.
Pages use the Page section. Content width sets a Narrow or Wide reading column. Headings, lists, quotes and links in your page content are styled to match the theme.

Oriel includes two page templates with sections already in place. Choose one in the page's Theme template setting in Shopify admin, then edit the sections in the theme editor: about: your page text, then a story with an image, three numbered values, a second image with text, and a link to shop. faq: your page text, then two groups of questions and answers marked up for search engines, and a link to your contact page. Keep the page's own text short, such as an introduction: the sections below it hold the rest. You can create more templates from the theme editor's template menu.

Create a page and choose the contact template in the page's Theme template setting. The Contact form section shows a subheading, the page title and your intro text beside the form, and can also show the page content and optional phone number and order number fields. Form heading sets the title above the form. Add Contact detail blocks for your email, phone, opening hours or helpful links: each one appears as a card with an icon you choose. The default contact template adds a Collapsible content section with quick answers below the form. Messages are sent to your store's email address.

Write your policies in Settings > Policies. Oriel shows each policy with breadcrumbs, a large title and spaced sections, beside a menu of all your policies (a row of buttons on phones). When your store has a page with the handle contact, a "Questions about our policies?" link to it appears under the menu. The footer links to your policies when Show policy links is on.

section: Page not found and password pages
text: The Page not found page offers search and links to your collections and home page. The Password page shows while your store is password protected. It can show your logo, a heading, the message you set in Online Store > Preferences and an email signup (Show email signup).
When a customer buys a gift card, the gift card page shows its value, code, a QR code to scan in store, a button to copy the code, Apple Wallet and printing.
Product pages The Product information section is made of blocks you can reorder, add or remove. Below it, Related products shows recommendations that Shopify creates automatically.

Block What it shows Title The product title. Show product type adds the type above it. Vendor The product's vendor. Price The price, with the compare-at price and percentage saved for products on sale, and the unit price where you've set one. Show tax and shipping note adds a line about taxes and shipping. Show Shop Pay Installments shows installment payments when they're available to your store. Variant picker Options as buttons or dropdowns (Style). Color options show the swatches you set for option values in Shopify admin. Options that are sold out or don't exist with the current selection

Products with selling plans (subscriptions, pre-orders or try before you buy) show Purchase options inside the buy buttons: one-time purchase, unless the product can only be bought with a plan, and each plan the selected variant supports, with its price and saving. The product price follows the chosen option. This works with the Shopify Subscriptions app and other apps that create selling plans; no app block is needed. The cart shows the plan name on each line.

Layout: Thumbnails shows one large image with thumbnails; Stacked shows images one under another. Image ratio: Portrait, Square or Adapt to image. Open images in a full-screen viewer: customers can click an image to view the gallery full screen. Autoplay videos: product videos play muted when they appear. On phones, images become a row customers can swipe through, with a counter. Selecting a variant shows its image.

Keep product information visible while scrolling: the details column stays in view next to long galleries on larger screens. Show add to cart bar on mobile: a bar with the price and add to cart button appears on phones once the main button scrolls out of view.
Collections and search

A collection page has two sections: Collection banner and Product grid. Collection banner shows the collection title, and optionally its image (Show collection image, Image height), description and product count. Edit the image and description in Products > Collections. Product grid sets Products per page, Columns on desktop, Columns on mobile and the product card options: Image ratio, Show second image on hover, Show add to cart button and Show product type badge.

Turn on Show filters and Show sorting in the Product grid section. Choose which filters appear in the Shopify Search & Discovery app: availability, price, product type, vendor, tags, variant options and metafields. Color filters show swatches. On larger screens, filters open as dropdowns above the products. On phones, they open in a drawer with a button that shows the number of results. Results update without reloading the page, and the address keeps the selected filters, so customers can share or bookmark them and use the back button. Selected filters appear as chips that customers can remove
The /collections page lists all your collections as tiles, with optional numbers.

The search window opens from the search icon in the header. With Show search suggestions on, it shows products, collections, pages and articles as customers type, with the matching words highlighted. Customers can move through suggestions with the arrow keys and press Enter to open one. The search results page can show Popular searches, and has the same filters and sorting as collection pages.
Quick add and cart

Turn on Show add to cart button in a section with product cards, such as Featured collection or Product grid. Products with a single variant show Add to bag and are added straight to the cart. Products with options, or with purchase options, show Choose options. It opens a panel where customers pick a variant, quantity and purchase option without leaving the page. View full details opens the product page with the chosen variant. On touch screens the button is always shown; on other screens it appears when customers hover over or focus the card.

Choose Cart type in Theme settings > Cart: Drawer: adding a product opens the cart in a panel at the side of the page. Page: customers stay where they are and see a short message with a link to the cart page.

Customers can change quantities and remove items. Removing an item offers Undo. If a customer asks for more than you have in stock, the cart shows the quantity available and explains why. Each line shows its options, subscription plan, discounts and unit price. Prices before a sale or subscription saving are crossed out. Show cart note adds an order note, in the cart drawer and on the cart page. Automatic discounts are shown on each line and in the total. Customers enter discount codes at checkout. On phones, the cart page shows a bar with the total and checkout button until the order summary
Languages and markets

Add countries in Settings > Markets. When you sell in more than one country, the footer shows a country/region selector (Show country/region selector in the footer section). Turn on Show currency codes in Theme settings > Currency format so customers can tell currencies with the same symbol apart.

Oriel's storefront text is translated into English, German, French, Spanish and Turkish, and the theme editor is available in English and Turkish. Add languages in Settings > Languages. When your store has more than one published language, the footer shows a language selector (Show language selector). To change any text in the theme, such as the button labels, go to Online Store > Themes > … > Edit default theme content.
Accessibility and performance

Oriel is built to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at level AA. Every control works with a keyboard and shows a visible focus outline. Menus, drawers, the search window and the image viewer are announced correctly by screen readers, and return focus to where the customer was when they close. Moving content can be paused, and stops for visitors who prefer reduced motion. Form errors appear under each field, in your store's language. To keep your store accessible: Add alt text to product images and other meaningful images. Keep enough contrast between text and background

Oriel loads only the code each page needs, sizes images for each screen and loads images further down the page as customers scroll. To keep your store fast: Upload images at least 2000 px wide, but compress them first: the file size matters more than the dimensions. Remove apps you no longer use. Many apps add code to every page. Keep the number of sections on your home page reasonable.

Frequently asked questions How do I change the fonts? In Theme settings > Typography. Choose fonts for headings, body text and accent text from Shopify's font library. How do I add a dropdown menu? In Content > Menus, drag a link under another link to nest it. Nested links open in a dropdown on larger screens and in the mobile menu. Why don't filters appear on my collection? Install the Shopify Search & Discovery app and add filters there. Check that Show filters is on in the Product grid section, and that your products have the information the filter uses, for example product types or variant
Support We help with questions about Oriel's features and settings, and we fix bugs in the theme. We reply within two business days.

Check the FAQ and the page of this guide about the feature you're using. If the problem started after you installed an app or edited code, try the same page in a fresh copy of Oriel from the Theme Store. If it works there, the app or the code change is the likely cause.

Help with the theme's settings, sections and features. Fixes for bugs in the theme. Support doesn't include custom design or code changes, problems caused by third-party apps or edited theme code, or setting up your store's products and content. For these, we recommend a Shopify Partner.
